correctness.rationale: Greedy complete-alphabet arch factorization proves every k-universal word has ≥qk symbols. For q>=3, (01...q−1)^(k−1)(0 2...q−1 1) is qk long and unbordered because any suffix beginning in 0 starts at a block boundary while nonempty block-aligned prefixes finish q−1 rather than 1. For binary length 2k, every arch is an opposite-bit pair; comparing first/last arches forces a border of length 1 or 2 when k>=2. A normalized extra-symbol first arch starts 001 and remaining arches pair, and explicit even/odd border comparison yields C_k constraints. Complements and reversals yield four disjoint families. Independent direct enumeration through k=7 recovered minimum lengths and counts k1..7: (2,2),(5,4),(7,4),(9,8),(11,12),(13,24),(15,44), with no shorter unbordered k-universal words. Infinite proof supplied by arch/border arguments.
residual_risks: No closed asymptotic expression for normalized C_k count; proofs do not cover cross-bifix-free sets or longer-than-minimal words.

final_claim: For alphabet size q>=3 and every k>=1 the shortest unbordered k-scattered-subsequence universal word has length qk. For binary, length is 2 at k=1 and 2k+1 for k>=2; all binary shortest witnesses are exactly T(c)=001 c1(1−c1)...c_(k−1)(1−c_(k−1)) and its bit-complement/reversal under explicit halfword border tests, with 4|C_k| witnesses.
